description: An opencode plugin that runs a task as a workflow with acceptance criteria, adversarial review and a completion gate.

glossary.Workflow: One task run through the phases intake, planning, execution, adversarial review, reconciliation and verification. A command such as /ultracode starts it.
glossary.Workflow record: The file .opencode/open-ultracode/state/workflow-state.json in the project root. It holds the goal, criteria, findings, evidence and completion report of one workflow.
glossary.Acceptance criterion: A statement that a command, a test or an observation can show to be true or false. Each has an ID such as AC-1.
glossary.Evidence: The recorded result of one check: pass, fail, blocked or not-run, with the acceptance criteria it proves.
glossary.Finding: A defect or gap that the adversarial review reports, with a severity, a confidence and evidence.
glossary.Completion gate: The rules that turn criteria, evidence and findings into one status: verified, partial, blocked, failed or research-only.
glossary.Coordinator: The session that ran the command. It keeps the workflow record and takes the final status from the completion gate.
glossary.Fusion: A run in which two panel agents on their own models answer, criticise and revise, and a decider chooses the result.
glossary.Research mode: The modes spec-audit and adversarial-research. They end in findings or a recommendation and report research-only.
